subject.title: Embedded agent: auto-rotate (or persist a marker) on context-overflow give_up instead of wedging the session until manual /reset

question: Should exhausted embedded-agent context-overflow recovery close this issue by landing the marker-first linked PR, or should maintainers require guarded auto-rotation/replay as the first supported recovery behavior?
rationale: Current source intentionally preserves manual recovery after overflow give-up, while the issue requests a new durable recovery contract or automatic replay behavior in core session state.

options.title: Land marker-first recovery
options.body: Accept the linked PR's durable blocked-run marker as the first recovery contract and leave automatic rotation for separate design work.

options.title: Require guarded auto-rotation
options.body: Keep this issue open until replay safety, loop caps, and pending-turn rotation semantics are implemented and proven.

options.title: Keep manual recovery only
options.body: Decline automatic recovery and limit the fix to diagnostics/docs if maintainers do not want new durable state or replay behavior.

recommendation.title: Land marker-first recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the linked PR's durable blocked-run marker as the first recovery contract and leave automatic rotation for separate design work.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is mainly a durable session-state and product-boundary choice, where recent history shows the strongest ownership signal.
